The multiplicity of a finite $\wp$-slope eigensystem does not increase when raising the level at $\wp$ from $\wp$ to $\wp^r$.

**Derivation.** Let $\lambda$ be a Hecke eigensystem of finite $\wp$-slope occurring in $S_k(\Gamma_1(\mathfrak{n}\wp))$. The inclusion of congruence subgroups $\Gamma_1(\mathfrak{n}\wp^r)\subset\Gamma_1(\mathfrak{n}\wp)$ induces degeneracy (oldform) maps
$$S_k(\Gamma_1(\mathfrak{n}\wp))\longrightarrow S_k(\Gamma_1(\mathfrak{n}\wp^r)).$$
On the $\lambda$-isotypic component, the $U_\wp$-operator acts with a eigenvalue of finite slope (hence invertibly on the relevant space). By the Drinfeld analogue of Atkin–Lehner oldform theory (Gekeler, Basson–Breuer–Pink, etc.), every cusp form in $S_k(\Gamma_1(\mathfrak{n}\wp^r))$ carrying the eigensystem $\lambda$ is an oldform coming from level $\Gamma_1(\mathfrak{n}\wp)$; no newforms of higher $\wp$-power level can share the same finite-slope eigensystem because the associated automorphic representation would then have conductor dividing $\mathfrak{n}\wp$, contradicting minimality. Moreover, the finite-slope condition ensures that among the various degeneracy maps only the natural inclusion-induced map contributes to $\lambda$, and it does so injectively with the same multiplicity. Thus the $\lambda$-eigenspace in $S_k(\Gamma_1(\mathfrak{n}\wp^r))$ is isomorphic to that in $S_k(\Gamma_1(\mathfrak{n}\wp))$, and the ratio of multiplicities is $1$.
